file: papers/pdf/Cattani - 2005 - Preadaptation Firm Heterogeneity and Technological Performance.pdf
about: The paper develops the notion of technological preadaptation—skills and knowledge a firm accumulated without foresight of later uses that by chance prove useful in a new domain—and shows in fiber optics (1970-1995) that having and especially leveraging such preadaptation raises technological performance.

candidates.label: Knowledge accumulated without foresight
candidates.definition: Preadaptation is the part of a firm's prior experience built up for reasons unrelated to, and without anticipation of, the later application in which it proves useful.
candidates.applies_when: An account describes skills, knowledge or assets developed for one purpose that later turned out to be useful for a new venture or domain nobody had anticipated at the time.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The knowledge was built deliberately after the new application was already known (adaptation, not preadaptation).

candidates.label: Chance usefulness for another function
candidates.definition: Borrowed from biology: a feature that works in one function turns out by chance to work in another after relatively little adjustment; no role is assigned to foresight.
candidates.applies_when: The person says something they had happened to fit a new use with only minor adjustment, stressing it was not planned for that use.

candidates.label: Adaptation vs preadaptation
candidates.definition: Efforts made after the new application is known (e.g., first lab experiments aimed at it) are adaptation, distinct from earlier unanticipated accumulation.
candidates.applies_when: A coder can distinguish whether relevant capabilities were built before versus after the person became aware of the new opportunity.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Use preadaptation only for pre-awareness accumulation; post-awareness targeted development is adaptation.

candidates.label: Watershed event revealing new use
candidates.definition: A dividing event (e.g., the 1966 paper showing glass could transmit data) marks when a new application becomes conceivable, after which foresight and market feedback begin to guide search.
candidates.applies_when: An account points to a specific event, publication or signal that suddenly made existing know-how relevant to a new possibility.

candidates.label: Leveraging (using) preadaptation
candidates.definition: Having relevant knowledge is distinct from actually drawing on it in the new domain; firms that build on their prior know-how perform better.
candidates.applies_when: The person describes actively redeploying earlier, unrelated experience into the new venture, not merely possessing it.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The person had the relevant prior experience but did not use it or used it late (having without using).

candidates.label: Recognising redeployment possibility
candidates.definition: The transition period is when a firm begins to realize it can redeploy pre-existing skills to a new domain; foresight and strategy matter most here.
candidates.applies_when: An account describes the moment of realizing that something one already had could be applied to a new opportunity.

candidates.label: Unrelated prior investments
candidates.definition: Past investments, even abandoned ones, can later prove useful, as Corning's divested integrated-circuit venture happened to supply knowledge for fiber optics.
candidates.applies_when: An account cites earlier projects, failed or divested ventures, or side activities whose knowledge later fed a new venture.

candidates.label: Antiquated or trapped knowledge reused
candidates.definition: Old technologies or knowledge that became a competency trap in its current use can become a source of advantage in a distinct domain.
candidates.applies_when: The person describes outdated or stagnating know-how finding a fresh, unanticipated application.

candidates.label: Transformative capacity and routines
candidates.definition: Firms with routines to store, transform and retrieve knowledge are better able to realize new syntheses from in-house solutions.
candidates.applies_when: An account mentions practices for keeping and retrieving past knowledge that enabled spotting or using an unexpected application.

candidates.label: Incentives shaping pursuit
candidates.definition: Equally preadapted firms differ in whether, when and how quickly they act; e.g., AT&T saw fiber as a substitute threatening its network, while Corning saw a new growth market, and ITT entered late despite doing the groundwork.
candidates.applies_when: The person explains acting on or ignoring a fortuitous fit because of existing business interests, incentives or timing.

candidates.label: Broad similarity of technological roots
candidates.definition: Transferability depends on similarity, but preadaptation can apply across domains that look entirely distinct to users yet share technological roots.
candidates.applies_when: An account notes that a seemingly unrelated market drew on the same underlying technical know-how.

candidates.label: Starting a new domain
candidates.definition: Redeployed preadapted knowledge can spur new technological fields or lineages when it taps unexploited niches with different needs.
candidates.applies_when: Prior unanticipated know-how is described as the basis for creating a new venture, market or field.

candidates.label: Superior performance and advantage
candidates.definition: Preadapted firms that consistently leveraged prior experience achieved higher technological performance; prior experience becomes advantage rather than constraint.
candidates.applies_when: An account links unanticipated prior experience to success or advantage in the new venture.

candidates.label: Strategic foresight
candidates.definition: Heterogeneity may stem from foresight rather than luck; realistically both play roles, and purposive behavior shows in differential leverage.
candidates.applies_when: The person attributes the fit to deliberate anticipation and planning rather than to chance.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: Do not code as rival when the person emphasizes the knowledge was built without foreseeing the use.

candidates.label: Pure luck of environment
candidates.definition: Raised and criticised: performance simply reflects random resource endowments that the environment happens to favor, leaving no role for strategy.
candidates.applies_when: The person explains success as merely being in the right place with the right resources, with no action of their own.

candidates.label: Complementary assets
candidates.definition: Success in a new domain may instead stem from possessing commercialization assets; the author treats this as not mutually exclusive.
candidates.applies_when: The account credits distribution, manufacturing or other commercial assets rather than unanticipated technical know-how.
